findings.title: Negative flusher_processes silently creates no flusher processes
findings.body: The --flusher-processes option is not validated as positive. If a negative value is supplied, SpanFlusher computes a negative num_processes, so range(num_processes) creates no process-to-shard map entries, no flusher processes, and self.buffers is empty. The consumer will still forward/commit messages, while flusher backpressure and Redis memory checks in submit() are skipped because there are no buffers. Validate or clamp flusher_processes to a positive value before constructing SpanFlusher.

findings.title: join() treats timeout=0 as no timeout
findings.body: join() computes deadline as time.time() + timeout if timeout else None. A timeout of 0 is falsy, so it is treated as no timeout and join can block indefinitely even though the caller requested a non-blocking join. Use `if timeout is not None` when computing the deadline.

findings.title: Flusher process health is only checked on submit
findings.body: _ensure_processes_alive() is only invoked from submit(). If the consumer is idle or not receiving new span batches, poll() will not detect or restart a crashed or hung flusher process, so already-buffered segments may remain unflushed until traffic arrives. Consider checking process health in poll() or another periodic hook.

findings.title: Added sleep in test is disabled by the test's own monkeypatch
findings.body: test_basic monkeypatches time.sleep to a no-op and then calls time.sleep(0.1) to wait for flusher threads. Because the patch is active, the call does not actually wait, so the test still relies on thread scheduling and may be flaky. Use the original sleep function, an event, or poll for the expected message instead.

findings.title: Kafka producer is not closed when the flusher loop raises
findings.body: In SpanFlusher.main, producer.close() is only reached if the loop terminates normally. If produce(), future.result(), or buffer.done_flush_segments() raises, the Kafka producer is not closed before the process exits or is restarted, leaking connections/file descriptors. Close the producer in a finally block.

findings.title: Unhealthy flusher process is replaced without joining/closing it
findings.body: When _ensure_processes_alive() kills an unhealthy process, it immediately starts a replacement without joining or closing the old process object. This can leave zombie processes/file descriptors and creates a short window where the old and replacement processes may both act on the same shards. Join/close the killed process, with a timeout if needed, before replacing it.

findings.title: join() may leave later flusher processes unterminated after timeout
findings.body: In join(), if the deadline is reached while waiting for one flusher process, the loop breaks and remaining processes are not terminated. With multiple flusher processes now present, shutdown can leave extra processes running. Terminate all processes even after the timeout expires, or restructure the loop so timeout does not skip termination of later processes.
